name: Front
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Operate a shared mailbox with assignments, comments, and simple rules

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Up to 10 seats; 1 workspace; 1 channel type; up to 10 channels/license; 10 automation rules; 200 AI compose/translate/summarize actions per teammate/day
tiers.notes: Billed annually; month-to-month USD rate was not published in the retrieved official page.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Up to 50 seats; 5 workspaces; omnichannel; up to 30 channels/license; 20 automation rules; 200 basic AI actions/teammate/day
tiers.notes: Billed annually; month-to-month USD rate was not published in the retrieved official page.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited workspaces/rules/macros; up to 50 channels/license; Copilot, Smart QA and Smart CSAT included
tiers.notes: Billed annually; no maximum seat count stated.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day Professional trial; no credit card required)
pricing.billingTerms: annual pricing published (24% saving); monthly billing control exists but current month-to-month USD figures were not exposed in official page text
pricing.hiddenCosts: Starter and Professional AI add-ons: Copilot $20/seat/month, Smart QA $20, Smart CSAT $10, QA+CSAT $25; Autopilot starts at $0.05/conversation. Native WhatsApp adds Meta charges plus a 20% admin fee; API capacity costs $200 per extra 100 requests/minute/month; contracts over $25,000 require paid onboarding.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Front, operate a shared mailbox with assignments, comments, and simple rules. The hard boundary is email infrastructure, many channels, workflow automation, crm context, and enterprise governance, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer messages into a shared mailbox, assign conversations, comment internally, apply simple rules, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
whatYouLose: email infrastructure, many channels, workflow automation, CRM context, and enterprise governance
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Front because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

facts.dataFormat: Conversations, contacts and configuration in PostgreSQL; Redis handles jobs and cache; attachments use local disk or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is support-inbox oriented and weaker than Front for email-first shared drafting, internal collaboration, routing rules and multi-inbox operations.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires a VM or Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, SMTP, persistent or object storage, HTTPS, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.desc: Email becomes an assigned team inbox with notes and collision warnings; the nicer modules open a wallet.

facts.install: Upload the PHP application and run its Laravel web installer
facts.dataFormat: Mailbox, ticket and contact data in MySQL or MariaDB; attachments in application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its rules, integrations, mobile experience and collaboration are less polished than Front's, and several useful modules are separately paid.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and a web server, MySQL or MariaDB, cron, IMAP or SMTP or OAuth, backups and separately paid modules for several extras

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A two-seat shared inbox and live chat bolted to a CRM; free until the limits become colleagues.

facts.dataFormat: Records and files live in HubSpot's cloud; CRM records can be exported as CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: Its shared inbox is a basic CRM feature, not Front's mature email-first assignment, commenting, drafting, rules and multi-inbox workspace.

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose, Portainer or OS package
facts.dataFormat: Tickets and users in PostgreSQL, queue and cache in Redis, search in Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, and attachments in filesystem or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It treats messages as help-desk tickets rather than preserving Front's lighter, email-native team collaboration model.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting normally means Docker plus PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, mail channels, a domain and backups

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets, email, and a help centre for zero dollars; the tiny tawk.to badge pays the rent.

facts.install: Hosted signup plus a JavaScript snippet or CMS plugin
facts.engines: tawk.to AI Assist; underlying models are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Chats, tickets and contacts live in tawk.to's cloud database until deleted; chat and ticket data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: It is chat-first and much weaker for shared email drafting, comments, assignments and rules than Front.
facts.setupBlocker: The website widget or plugin must be installed; removing tawk.to branding is paid

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free Help Desk
alternatives.desc: A hosted shared inbox, live chat, and ticket queue for two users; the knowledge base lives upstairs.

facts.dataFormat: Tickets, inbox messages and contact records live in HubSpot's cloud; records can be exported as CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a basic ticket and inbox queue rather than Front's polished email-first collaboration, shared drafting and rule system.

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

facts.dataFormat: Tickets, messages and attachments live in Odoo Online's managed database and filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: It is ticket-centric and lacks Front's fluid shared-mailbox collaboration, drafting, comments and email automation.
facts.setupBlocker: None for Helpdesk alone; installing another Odoo app ends the one-app-free arrangement

alternatives.name: LibreDesk
alternatives.desc: A modern email-and-live-chat desk in one compact stack, because apparently that was allowed.

facts.install: Docker or prebuilt binary with PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Conversations, contacts, rules and settings in PostgreSQL; attachments live on the self-hosted instance or configured storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a much younger product with a smaller integration, mobile, reporting and administration ecosystem than Front.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker or a binary plus PostgreSQL, mail channels, a domain, HTTPS, persistent storage and backups

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeScout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The shared mailbox is free; the rules that make it Front-like are a paid module.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Freshdesk Free Program
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The no-cost program expires after six months; that is a trial with better manners.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Front in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer messages into a shared mailbox, assign conversations, comment internally, apply simple rules, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
